evidence.testTitle: [SVC-005 SVC-006 SVC-007 SVC-008 SVC-009 SVC-010 SVC-011 SVC-013 SVC-017] F aliases enforce rank and persistent grant removal after recreation
evidence.scenarioScope: F rank and privilege observations with repeated ordinary-user denial after recreation.
evidence.rationale: Actual frozen Worker SQLite with independent authenticated accounts and real IRC and REST entrypoints.
assertionDetails: Real F OP, DEOP, VOICE and DEVOICE produce MODE; lower-rank requests and founder-target DEOP are denied, and founder/outsider IRC and event streams have public delivery barriers.
After recreation the ordinary member is again denied founder-rank or voice elevation, and unrelated channel grant and member grant absence are read from SQLite.
Founder creates a REST role and issues IRC MODE controls; an ordinary member is denied the corresponding privileged actions, including IRC MODE after recreation.
Exact successful aliases exercised are F OP, PRIVMSG F :DEOP, F VOICE and PRIVMSG F :DEVOICE; direct F CHANLEV and PRIVMSG F :CHANLEV are separately executed.

evidence.testTitle: [SVC-010 SVC-011 SVC-012 SVC-013] actual F and ChanServ persistent removals survive independent recreations
evidence.scenarioScope: Separate recreations after each F and ChanServ grant and removal.
evidence.rationale: Actual frozen Worker SQLite with independent authenticated accounts and real IRC and REST entrypoints.
assertionDetails: For both actual F CHANLEV and CS AMODE, real grants persist through recreation and authorized F and REST controls, then removal immediately rejects F OP, REST info PATCH and REST role creation.
Each immediate and post-recreation denial has its own IRC and event subscriber window bounded by real positive message barriers; no misleading MODE or events are observed.

Independent read-only SQLite reads compare exact channel_permissions rows in #grants and #sentinel immediately before and after every denial, preserve sentinel across transitions, and confirm the granted state and removed baseline across independent runtime recreations.

evidence.testTitle: [SVC-001 SVC-002 SVC-003 SVC-004 SVC-014 SVC-015] service authentication and identity gates retain independent grants after restart
evidence.scenarioScope: Independent service authentication, selected negative controls and their post-recreation repetition.
evidence.rationale: Actual frozen Worker SQLite with independent authenticated accounts and real IRC and REST entrypoints.
assertionDetails: Unauthenticated service commands, invalid NickServ/F authentication, reserved service nicknames, dropping Alice nickname and unauthorized registration are rejected.
Founder unregisters and reregisters; member cannot register unregistered channel, and a real F JOIN provides a positive control. A forged F prefix is delivered with Bob identity.
IRC and event observers have message barriers around denial sequence; final SQLite verifies account nick ownership and independent channel grant.
After recreation a fresh guest and separately authenticated Bob repeat the corresponding selected authentication, identity and registration denials.

evidence.testTitle: [SVC-001 SVC-002 SVC-003 SVC-004 SVC-014 SVC-015] service authentication and identity gates retain independent grants after restart
evidence.scenarioScope: Independent service authentication, selected negative controls and their post-recreation repetition.
evidence.rationale: Actual frozen Worker SQLite with independent authenticated accounts and real IRC and REST entrypoints.
assertionDetails: Real F AUTH with Bob own password succeeds, while F AUTH alice with the wrong password and NickServ invalid credential attempts fail; the F invalid request repeats after recreation.
Independent account nickname ownership and unrelated grants persist; denial recipient windows have IRC and event barriers.

evidence.testTitle: [SVC-001 SVC-002 SVC-003 SVC-004 SVC-014 SVC-015] service authentication and identity gates retain independent grants after restart
evidence.scenarioScope: Actual NickServ grouping and account registration attempts against another account nickname.
evidence.rationale: Actual frozen Worker SQLite with independent authenticated accounts and real IRC and REST entrypoints.
assertionDetails: Bob successfully groups his own BobExtra nickname; NICK alice is rejected as belonging to Alice, NS GROUP alice acts on BobExtra rather than transferring Alice, and unauthorized NS SAREGISTER alice is rejected.

An IRC and event denial window surrounds the attack; after recreation Bob repeats the nickname, grouping and registration attacks, and SQLite identifies Alice as owner of alice and Bob as owner of bob and bobextra.
No claim that GROUP accepts a target: its argument is ignored, and the authenticated current nickname is the actual target.
